plan: I will bid my true value, $39. In this 3-bidder third-price auction the winner pays the lowest of the three bids, so if I win my profit is 39 − min(opponents' bids). Bidding above 39 risks winning when the lowest opponent bid exceeds 39 (negative profit); bidding below 39 forgoes profitable wins. With no history and independent draws, truthful bidding balances these risks and maximizes expected long-run profit. Bid must be in $0.1 increments.

[Value = 27. In a 3-bidder third-price auction the winner pays the lowest opponent bid, so raising my bid increases win probability without changing the price I pay. With no history, assume opponents’ bids aren’t always very high; maximizing win probability tends to raise expected profit. To capture most positive surplus cases while accepting the risk both opponents are very high, bid the maximum to ensure winning and realize the expected gap between 27 and the opponents' minimum bid.]

[Assume opponents bid their private values uniformly on [0,49]. If I bid b, P(win)=(b/49)^2 and conditional E[min(b2,b3)|both<b]=b/3. Expected profit = (13 - b/3)*(b/49)^2, maximized at b=26. So I overbid my value to raise win probability while keeping expected payment tied to opponents' lower bids. ]
